metadata.disclaimer: Always refer to official BMW TIS documentation for complete procedures. This guide is for reference only.

bmw_specific_tools.usage: Locks crankshaft at TDC during timing service
bmw_specific_tools.notes: Insert through hole in bell housing

required_for: Valve cover replacement with integrated sensor

bmw_specific_tools.usage: Compresses oil pump chain tensioner for installation
Guides front seal onto crankshaft without damage
Holds crankshaft during harmonic balancer removal
Safely removes fuel injectors from fuel rail
Factory diagnostic system for fault reading and programming

head_bolts.sequence: Start from center, work outward in spiral pattern
head_bolts.notes: Always use new bolts. Follow exact sequence.

camshaft_bearing_caps.notes: Tighten evenly to avoid camshaft bind

crankshaft_pulley_bolt.notes: Plus additional full turn. Use holding tool.

exhaust_manifold_nuts.notes: Replace copper sealing nuts if worn

warnings: Do not mix with other coolant types

automatic_transmission.notes: Requires special fill procedure with temperature monitoring

power_steering_fluid.notes: Some models have electric power steering (no fluid)

steps: Warm engine to operating temperature (5 min drive)
Position vehicle on level surface, engage parking brake
Remove underbody panel if equipped
Position drain pan under oil pan
Remove drain plug (17mm) and allow oil to drain completely
Install new drain plug washer and reinstall plug (25 Nm)
Remove oil filter cap with filter wrench
Remove old filter element from cap
Install new filter element into cap, ensure O-rings are seated
Reinstall filter cap (25 Nm)
Add 6.0L oil through filler cap
Start engine, check for leaks
Stop engine, wait 2 minutes, check level
Add oil as needed to bring to full mark
Reset oil service indicator via iDrive or ISTA
notes: Do not overtorque drain plug - aluminum pan threads easily
Replace filter cap O-rings if damaged
Always verify oil level after running engine

steps: Remove engine cover (pull up at rear)
Disconnect negative battery terminal
Locate VANOS solenoids on front of cylinder head
Disconnect electrical connectors (press tab, pull)
Remove solenoid mounting bolt (E10)
Pull solenoid straight out - may require gentle prying
Inspect solenoid screen filter - clean or replace if clogged
Lubricate new O-ring with clean engine oil
Install new solenoid, ensure proper orientation
Install and torque mounting bolt (8 Nm)
Reconnect electrical connector until click
Repeat for other solenoid if needed
Reconnect battery
Start engine and verify smooth operation
Clear fault codes with ISTA/scan tool
Perform VANOS adaptation reset if available
notes: Solenoids can often be cleaned and reinstalled
Always inspect filter screens for debris
Replace both solenoids if one fails (preventive)

valve_cover_gasket_replacement.special_considerations: Late model N52s have integrated eccentric shaft sensor
tools_required: Eccentric shaft tool (11-3-450) for late models
parts_required: New valve cover (if cracked/warped) or gasket kit
steps: Disconnect negative battery terminal
Remove engine cover
Remove ignition coils (E10 bolts, pull straight up)
Disconnect all electrical connectors from valve cover
Label and photograph connector locations
Disconnect VANOS solenoid connectors
Disconnect eccentric shaft sensor connector
Remove CCV hoses from valve cover
Remove valve cover bolts (T30) in reverse of torque sequence
Carefully lift valve cover - may be stuck from old gasket
Clean all gasket mating surfaces thoroughly
Inspect valve cover for cracks or warpage
Install new spark plug tube seals into valve cover
Install new main gasket into valve cover groove
Apply small bead of RTV at cam cap/head joints (half moons)
Position valve cover and hand-start all bolts
Torque bolts in sequence from center outward (10 Nm)
Reinstall all components in reverse order
Reconnect battery
Start engine, check for leaks
Perform eccentric shaft sensor adaptation if replaced
notes: Late models may require eccentric shaft position reset with ISTA
Do not overtorque valve cover bolts - will crack cover
Complete valve cover replacement often more reliable than gasket only

parts_required: Fresh BMW blue coolant (at least 4 liters)
steps: Allow engine to cool completely
Disconnect negative battery terminal
Remove underbody panel for access
Place drain pan under radiator
Open radiator drain cock or remove lower hose to drain coolant
Remove air intake duct for access
Disconnect electrical connector from water pump
Remove water pump mounting bolts (3x T30 or E10)
Carefully remove pump - coolant will drain
Clean mounting surface on engine
Install new O-ring, lightly lubricated with coolant
Install new pump, align correctly
Install and torque mounting bolts (10 Nm)
Reconnect electrical connector
Reinstall any removed components
Close radiator drain
Fill coolant system using spill-free funnel
Fill slowly, allowing air to escape
Start engine with cap off, continue filling
Cycle heater to full hot to bleed heater core
Monitor temperature, top off coolant as needed
Install expansion tank cap when system is full and bled
Reconnect battery
Test drive, monitor temperature gauge
Recheck coolant level when cold
notes: Electric pump may run with ignition on, engine off - this is normal
Bleed procedure critical - air pockets cause overheating
Consider replacing thermostat at same time (preventive)

tools_required: 14mm spark plug socket with rubber insert
steps: Allow engine to cool (plugs easier to remove when cool)
Remove engine cover
Disconnect ignition coil connectors
Remove ignition coil mounting bolts (E10)
Pull ignition coils straight up and out
Use compressed air to blow debris from spark plug wells
Remove spark plugs using 14mm spark plug socket
Inspect old plugs for condition (wear, deposits, damage)
Gap new plugs to 0.8mm if not pre-gapped
Apply thin coat of anti-seize to plug threads
Install new plugs by hand first to avoid cross-threading
Torque plugs to 25 Nm
Reinstall ignition coils
Reconnect coil connectors
Reinstall engine cover
Start engine, verify smooth operation
notes: OEM plugs last 60,000 miles typically
Do not over-tighten - aluminum head threads easily
Replace coils if plug wells have oil (from bad tube seals)

steps: Allow engine to cool completely
Disconnect negative battery terminal
Drain coolant via radiator drain or lower hose
Remove air intake duct for access
Disconnect electrical connector from thermostat housing
Remove coolant hoses from thermostat housing (mark positions)
Remove thermostat housing mounting bolts
Remove housing with thermostat
Clean mounting surface on cylinder head
Install new thermostat housing assembly
Torque mounting bolts (10 Nm)
Reconnect coolant hoses with new clamps if needed
Reconnect electrical connector
Refill and bleed cooling system (see water pump procedure)
Start engine, monitor for leaks and proper temperature operation
notes: Electronic thermostat requires proper operation for emissions
Fault codes may set if thermostat doesn't reach target temp
Often done with water pump as preventive maintenance

parts_required: Oil filter housing gasket set (includes all O-rings)
steps: Drain engine oil (or be prepared for spillage)
Disconnect negative battery terminal
Remove engine cover and air intake components for access
Remove oil filter cap and filter
Disconnect any sensors/lines attached to housing
Remove oil filter housing mounting bolts
Remove housing (may require wiggling due to O-ring seal)
Remove old gasket and all O-rings from housing and block
Clean all sealing surfaces thoroughly
Install new O-rings on housing (lubricate with oil)
Install new main gasket
Position housing and install mounting bolts
Torque bolts evenly (10 Nm)
Install new oil filter and cap
Reinstall all removed components
Top off oil to proper level
Start engine, check for leaks thoroughly
Recheck after heat cycle
notes: Common leak point - oil can drip onto alternator
Replace all O-rings in the kit
Check oil cooler lines for leaks as well

diagnostic_steps: Read fault codes with BMW ISTA or compatible scanner
Check oil level and condition (low oil affects VANOS)
Inspect VANOS solenoid connectors for damage/corrosion
Check VANOS solenoid resistance (7-8.5 ohms)
Remove and inspect solenoid filter screens
With scanner, command VANOS advance/retard and monitor actual vs target
If solenoids pass electrical tests, internal wear may be issue
Check timing chain tension (excessive stretch affects VANOS operation)
Read fault codes with ISTA
Check eccentric shaft sensor connection
Perform eccentric shaft position test with ISTA
Check Valvetronic motor operation (listen for motor movement)
Verify motor electrical connection
Check for binding in eccentric shaft
With late models, verify valve cover is not cracked (sensor mount)
Visual inspection for coolant leaks
Pressure test cooling system (1.5 bar max)
Check expansion tank cap seal
Verify water pump operation (scan tool can command pump on)
Check thermostat operation (monitor temp rise pattern)
Verify no air pockets (repeat bleed if necessary)
Inspect water pump electrical connector
Check temperature sensor readings vs actual (infrared thermometer)
Read fault codes to identify affected cylinder(s)
Check spark plugs condition and gap
Test ignition coils (swap with known good)
Check fuel injector operation (resistance, spray pattern)
Compression test affected cylinder
Check for vacuum leaks (smoke test)
Verify MAF sensor readings
Check for intake manifold leaks (DISA valve area)

steps: Turn ignition to ON (do not start engine)
Navigate to Vehicle Information menu
Select Vehicle Status
Select Service Required
Select Reset
Confirm reset
Turn ignition OFF
Press and hold odometer reset button
While holding, turn ignition to ON
Continue holding until service message appears
Release button, then press and hold again
Message will reset when held for several seconds

battery_registration.description: Register new battery with vehicle computer
steps: Connect BMW ISTA or compatible tool
Navigate to Service Functions > Battery
Select Register Battery Replacement
Enter new battery specifications (Ah rating, type)
Complete registration
Vehicle will adjust charging strategy for new battery
battery_registration.notes: Required to prevent overcharging or undercharging new battery

steps: Clear all adaptation values with ISTA
Turn ignition off for 10 seconds
Turn ignition on, do not start
Wait 60 seconds for adaptation
Start engine, let idle for 5 minutes
Drive vehicle through various RPM ranges

vanos_adaptation.description: Reset VANOS adaptation after solenoid service
steps: Connect ISTA diagnostic system
Navigate to Service Functions > Engine
Select VANOS Adaptation
Follow on-screen procedure
May require engine running test
vanos_adaptation.notes: May clear on its own after several drive cycles
